newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends little changed from NY close.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends little changed from NY close.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended practically unchanged from its New York close in lacklustre trading marked only by some bargain hunting from physical buyers, gold dealers and traders said on Wednesday.
But most players sat on the sidelines, stunned by the unexpected slump in New York overnight, gold dealers said.
"There was absolutely no rebound, people don't have any confidence to buy," said Swiss Bank Corp.'s chief bullion dealer Anderson Cheung.
Gold traders in the territory said they had expected a small correction following the over-the-counter options expiry on Tuesday, but were not prepared for the sharp drop.
Gold traded in a new range from US$379.50 to $382 an ounce, with resistence at $382 and strong support at $380, traders said.
"There was no follow through on silver or anything in our time zone," said anther gold dealer at an international bank.
Gold dealers said they would wait to see what the market did next and could not reach a consensus on its direction.
Bullion ended at US$380.40/380.90 an ounce Wednesday against New York's US$380.35/85 close on Tuesday.
Local gold ended HK$18 lower at HK$3,508 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -3 from its previous fix at -5.50.
